title: Ecru reports prescribed burn near Toccopola as county burn ban continues
excerpt: The state lists Pontotoc County’s ban through Friday, Nov. 20. Its three exemptions leave household brush piles and backyard fire pits under the ban.
locality: Pontotoc County, Mississippi, including the Thaxton and Toccopola area.

facts.statement: The Town of Ecru identified smoke in the Thaxton and Toccopola area Tuesday as coming from a prescribed burn. Pontotoc County’s wider burn ban remains in effect. On Wednesday, the Mississippi Forestry Commission still listed Friday, Nov. 20, as the end date for the county order.
facts.evidence: Town describes a prescribed burn in the Thaxon/Toccopola area and shared a photograph of a smoke plume. Thaxton is the local town spelling. The live county table shows Pontotoc, 10/20/26, 11/20/26, codes 1, 2 and 4.
facts.date_context: Ecru notice Nov. 17, checked Nov. 18. State table on Nov. 18 lists the order through Nov. 20, 2026.
facts.locality: Pontotoc County, Mississippi, including the Thaxton and Toccopola area.
facts.identities: Town of Ecru and Mississippi Forestry Commission.

facts.statement: Ecru said prescribed burns can reduce vegetation that would otherwise fuel larger fires. Pontotoc County’s order exempts the Forestry Commission and certified burn managers. A third exemption covers commercial contractors using heavy construction equipment when their burns meet state environmental regulations.
facts.evidence: Town explains why prescribed burning can be used during a ban. County row codes 1, 2 and 4 match the named categories on the commission’s exemption key. Neither the operator nor an acreage is claimed.

paragraphs.text: The Town of Ecru identified smoke in the Thaxton and Toccopola area Tuesday as coming from a prescribed burn. Pontotoc County’s wider burn ban remains in effect. On Wednesday, the Mississippi Forestry Commission still listed Friday, Nov. 20, as the end date for the county order.

Ecru said prescribed burns can reduce vegetation that would otherwise fuel larger fires. Pontotoc County’s order exempts the Forestry Commission and certified burn managers. A third exemption covers commercial contractors using heavy construction equipment when their burns meet state environmental regulations.

Residents clearing yards still have to leave brush piles unburned. The commission also lists fire pits, burn barrels and campfires among the activities covered by a ban. It says orders expire at midnight on the listed date. Its county table is the place to check for an extension before making weekend plans.
